source: RFC 0013 B2b (the family bound under a burst)
statement: A family holds at most its bound plus the smaller of its bound and 4,096 entries of each kind (documents; entries for documents the store does not hold), plus the entries being installed or loaded at that moment; an install that finds its kind over that evicts at most 64 entries of that kind on the installing thread before it answers its waiters, which takes it back within the cap, and housekeeping evicts the rest. Evictions never take a kind below its bound, and passes running at once leave a kind at its bound when every victim was idle: they never stop above it.
guards: runtime:SnapshotFamilyBoundTest#a burst with housekeeping held never holds more than the cap, and the installer evicted it in place
runtime:SnapshotFamilyBoundTest#installs within the cap leave eviction to housekeeping, which takes the family back to its bound
runtime:SnapshotFamilyBoundTest#passes at once take a kind exactly to its bound, never below it and never stopping above it
runtime:SnapshotFamilyBoundTest#a victim whose kind changed between the choice and the removal is not removed, and no count moves
runtime:AbsentBoundWindowTest#members loading when the last pass scans are evicted once their loads end absent again
runtime:AbsentBoundWindowTest#a victim the pass chose that starts a load before its eviction is taken is evicted once that load ends
runtime:AbsentBoundWindowTest#an eviction whose transition throws is taken back to the bound by the next revalidation
runtime:InstallEvictionBoundTest#an install over the cap evicts a bounded batch in place, and housekeeping takes the family to its bound
runtime:InstallEvictionBoundTest#absent entries over the cap are evicted the same way, on the thread that installs them
